lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs' season is in the books at 32-36-14, and the conversation has moved squarely to what comes next. They finished 8th in atlantic division - a final placement that frames every decision this summer. The work now runs through the draft table, the trade market and the cap sheet, and the bets made over the next few weeks will shape the roster that shows up to camp. The next headline here comes from the front office, not the scoreboard. The NHL calendar has flipped to building season - draft prep, trade talks, and the roster surgery that shapes the next contending window. For the Toronto Maple Leafs, the work runs from the draft table to the trade market, and the choices made this summer will define the next window.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The Jays have spent the last three nights getting shoved around by the Yankees, and the latest thump landed hard - an 8-3 loss on June 14 that left Toronto staring at a 34-38 record, 3rd place in the AL East, and 10 games back. That is not the profile of a club controlling its own fate; it is a team trying to stop the slide before it becomes a crater. The brief spark on June 12, when Toronto beat New York 8-5, already feels like a flicker rather than a turn. Since then, the offense has gone quiet again, and the two-game skid has only sharpened the pressure on a roster that cannot afford many more empty nights. There is no hiding the math: a -2.0 mark and a.472 pace means the Jays need cleaner innings, more authoritative at-bats, and less self-inflicted damage. Caballero's clock antics may have added spice to the rivalry, but the standings still tell the real story. Tuesday in Boston brings the next checkpoint - a 5:45 p.m. ET start against the Red Sox, and another chance to prove this club still has some pulse.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: Something real has finally settled over Toronto - the noise of the chase is gone, and what remains is the hard accounting of a season that ended at 46-36, third in the Atlantic, respectable on paper and unfinished in spirit. Collin Murray-Boyles' transcendent rookie season gave the Raptors a young pillar and a clear reason to believe the rebuild is not drifting, but belief is not a plan. The numbers say they were 10 games out, with a final 5.0-point profile and a W1 finish, and that is the profile of a team that could win enough nights without ever looking like it had solved the bigger problem. Now comes the clean-up work - coaching, roster construction, and the draft board - with the draft dark horses, MELEEK THOMAS and QUADIR COPELAND, looming as the sort of swing choices that can sharpen or blunt the next two years. The old OG Anunoby trade chatter has new life after his Finals game-winner, too, because Toronto's past keeps poking at its present. What matters next is whether the front office turns a promising season into a more dangerous one - or just another promising story.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The offseason in Washington is no place for soft edges - especially when the roster is still being redrawn around a quarterback who has to make the whole operation look larger than it is. The loudest early-summer note is Jordan Magee and Percy Butler fighting for relevance in '26, a battle that tells you exactly where this team is: the middle class of the roster is under siege, and nobody is getting a free pass. Washington finished 3rd in the NFC East, 6 games back, with a W1 ending to a season that is now closed for business, so the real drama has shifted to who fits the next version of the club. Nick Cross slots in at No. 8 in the safety rankings, which only sharpens the pressure on Butler, while the Stefon Diggs admission has added a little heat to a receiver room that needs certainty, not theater. And if the Brandon Aiyuk rumble is more than background noise, Washington will have to decide whether it is watching from the porch or making a move. For now, the most important thing is who separates in minicamp - and who gets left behind.
